description: Curated synthetic narrative cases. All organisations, advisories, credentials and personal data are fictional. Reference replay calibrates the harness; it is not live-model evidence. The assess cases (E11-5) give an advisory, what its fix changed, Aegis's search of the code and a few lines of it, answered called, not called or can't tell with what a reviewer should check; the look-for cases give an advisory and its fix, answered with the names to search the code for.

reference.risk: Crafted requests may execute code through ledger-lib 1.0.0.
reference.impact: Code execution could compromise the internet-facing Payments API; exploitation is not confirmed.
actions: Confirm whether vulnerable requests reached the service and run its tests.

cases.title: Relevant supporting evidence is in a later grounding passage
cases.context:
Synthetic feed background: this example describes a library maintenance history rather than a production event. The feed records several releases and the publisher's review process. Earlier entries describe supported runtime platforms, test coverage and packaging metadata. There is no claim of exploitation at an entity in these background entries. The release history includes routine changes to compatibility tests, examples and error messages. Those details do not themselves establish an affected service or an appropriate upgrade target. The matching and scoring inputs are supplied separately by Aegis and remain deterministic. The published release notes distinguish source-level changes from deployment-specific impact. A package being available does not establish that a service deployed it. Reviewers use the service inventory and the selected manifest to determine what actually changes. This synthetic background deliberately occupies the first passage so the relevant service facts are preserved and cited from a later passage. The draft still needs to explain the intended change and its validation.
Affected service: Export API uses stream-lib 1.0.0 in requirements.txt. Aegis selected 2.1.0 as the safe target for synthetic CVE-2099-0010. Review release notes and run the Export API tests before merging.

reference.content: Draft for Export API: upgrade stream-lib from 1.0.0 to Aegis-selected 2.1.0 in requirements.txt. Review release notes and run the Export API tests before merging.

cases.advisory: Synthetic CVE-2099-0007: lodash-like before 4.17.21 allows command injection through template() when the template string comes from an attacker. merge() and other functions are not affected.

excerpts.text:
import { merge } from 'lodash';
export const config = merge(defaults, overrides);

reference.rationale: render passes request input (req.body.view) to template, the function the advisory names.

cases.title: A type-shaped trigger the whole codebase never declares
cases.advisory: Synthetic CVE-2099-0012: jackson-like before 2.18.10 lets a java.nio.file.Path field bound from untrusted JSON load an arbitrary FileSystemProvider under the default JsonMapper.builder().build().
cases.fix_summary: src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/ext/NioPathDeserializer.java: changed in public Path deserialize(JsonParser p, DeserializationContext ctxt)

reference.rationale: The code binds JSON with a default ObjectMapper, the vulnerable setup, but a complete search of 64 files found no java.nio.file.Path, so no bound class can hold the Path field that triggers it.

cases.advisory: Synthetic CVE-2099-0012: jackson-like before 2.18.10 lets a java.nio.file.Path field bound from untrusted JSON load an arbitrary FileSystemProvider under the default JsonMapper.builder().build().

reference.rationale: The controller binds the request body into Upload, whose attachment field is a java.nio.file.Path: the type the advisory says triggers it.
